focus: Identify high-value semantic checks elsewhere in .skilled and define default-on integration requirements, cost, and risks.
noveltyJustification: This pass identifies two concrete adjacent use cases and reconciles the model arm's current opt-in/zero-call contract with the operational, privacy, status, and cost requirements of a default-on production path.
keyQuestions: Where in .skilled could claim-to-evidence semantic review add useful signal beyond lexical or path/line checks?
What would a default-on semantic integration require operationally, what is its call/latency cost, and what risks need controls?
Which existing contract would default-on behavior change?
answeredQuestions: AC_COVERAGE evidence support is a high-value semantic check; goal-criteria lint is a close sibling and already has an opt-in Jev arm.
Default-on requires an intentional amendment to the zero-call contract, production corpus/mode, provider and privacy controls, bounded budget, visible status, and advisory human review.
Observed benchmark cost is 121 calls/40 rows with 326/423ms p50/p95; 3N+1 is the measured design's call formula, and USD cost is unknown.
ruledOut: Treating the 40-row labeled benchmark as the gold set for every current in-range citation.
Letting a semantic flag replace deterministic dead-citation results or automatically block/repair a document.
Treating a skipped invocation's exit code 0 as evidence of semantic success.
nextFocus: Synthesize evidence, cost model, recommended improvements, adjacent use cases, and unresolved privacy/holdout questions.

title: Semantic review can test whether AC evidence supports its criterion
finding: AC_COVERAGE checks file:line presence and resolution, not semantic relevance; even an unresolved citation can count toward coverage. An advisory Jev pass could prioritize resolved evidence for Tested/Partially covered criteria.
inference: Semantic evidence support should catch locators that exist but do not demonstrate the criterion; labeled adjudication against AC statuses would confirm useful precision.

title: Goal criteria lint already offers a close semantic evaluation pattern
finding: The goal-criteria lint evaluates self-contained/checkable criteria and already has an opt-in Jev arm with labeled data, confidence intervals, and stale-label reporting; reuse its evaluation lessons rather than duplicating the evaluator.
inference: A shared evaluation harness could reduce duplicated label, uncertainty, and cost-reporting code; cross-feature parity would confirm portability.

title: Default-on calls would change the zero-call public contract
finding: The current feature promises zero calls by default and requires explicit --jev plus --out. A default-on semantic path needs deliberate contract, CLI, privacy, provider, and opt-out changes, separate from the deterministic scanner.
inference: Changing default behavior without updating the documented contract would surprise existing zero-call users; explicit contract review would confirm the intended rollout.

title: Use per-run call budgets and expose the scale assumption
finding: Current design costs 3N+1 planned calls before retries; the measured 40-row benchmark used 121 calls. Applying that pattern to a prior 208-in-range census would be 625 calls, an unmeasured extrapolation.
inference: Actual production cost depends on current eligible rows, backend billing, and retry rate; a full current census and an approved rate card would confirm it.

title: Skipped and partial arms need explicit machine status
finding: The Jev gate checks a pinned version and credentials; timeouts/retries are per call and a skipped/stopped arm can still exit 0. Default-on needs explicit completed/skipped/partial/failed status, visible budget and circuit breaker.
inference: Explicit statuses make missing semantic coverage distinguishable from a clean result; integration acceptance criteria can validate that distinction.

title: Provider receives sentence, path, and cited window
finding: The semantic request sends repository content to the configured backend. Default-on use needs path allowlists, data minimization/redaction, provider approval, retention rules, audit controls, and a resolution of the discrepancy between the packet's log note and the inspected local logger.
inference: Provider-side retention and contents of the historical artifact are not established by local caller code; the run artifact and provider/runtime retention terms would confirm them.

title: Keep semantic flags advisory pending independent holdout
finding: The 40-row benchmark is too small to justify automatic edits or blocking validation. Keep deterministic resolution independent and route semantic uncertainty to a human until a representative held-out evaluation supports a threshold.
inference: A larger live-only holdout and predeclared operating threshold would confirm whether automated enforcement is justified.
